question: Explain how the business's casual employment of van operators could be contributing to its turnover.
studentResponse: If you never know whether you will get shifts next week, you keep looking for something steadier, and the day something steady turns up you are gone. That is the position of Kerbside's van staff, and every time one walks out the owners pay again to find and train the next person.

ladder.text: Because casual van operators have no guaranteed hours, they lack job security and continue searching for more stable work.

ladder.text: Van operators who cannot rely on regular shifts will seek steadier employment and resign when they find it.
Without guaranteed hours, casual van operators are motivated to seek alternative, more secure employment, increasing the likelihood they will voluntarily leave the business.

The absence of guaranteed hours under casual contracts creates persistent job insecurity for van operators, incentivising them to seek permanent roles and voluntarily exit Kerbside once a more secure position is found.
